repairs.value: Strongest feature: The science comparison precisely distinguishes distrust of isolated, motivated reasoners from confidence in institutional reasoning, explaining how organized disconfirmation converts reciprocal criticism into a more reliable collective process. Principal limitation: The transcript illustrates the mechanism and reports selective evidence-search, but it does not establish how reliably particular institutional arrangements defeat shared biases, conformity, or systematically unchallenged assumptions. Live burden: Haidt must specify which adversarial structures make correction dependable and show their relevance to moral inquiry, while his diagnostic point need not independently settle the separate philosophical dispute over moral truth. Locked score: The resolved 88 appropriately rewards a coherent, responsive institutional account and unusually clear individual-versus-system distinction, while preserving a meaningful deduction for empirical uncertainty about when correction actually succeeds.
